Its integrated, centered quantile curves supply each candidate residual shape and amplitude to sequential sampled-maxima selection.

This ports the evaluated amplitude construction from the filtered-input donor onto the adapted Parent. Earlier siblings replaced native shape with Gaussian shape or removed query-only coordinates; this experiment keeps both and tests whether changing amplitude improves full and late productive gains.

finding_summary.headline: GP amplitude changed purchases and raised late gain, but reduced full gain and endpoint score.
finding_summary.insights:
This result rules out the exact claim that substituting GP amplitude transfers a joint full- and late-gain benefit to the adapted native host. Missing feedback, nonexecution and unchanged selections cannot explain that failure. The loss is concentrated earlier in search: first-100-purchase gain falls from 7.9045 to 5.5581, while the final-90-purchase gain rises from 1.8988 to 2.5079. There are slightly more parent-beating purchases overall, 713 versus 697, but their total improvement is smaller; counts and late recovery therefore cannot substitute for productive mass or endpoints. On the same paid labels, mean 90% predictive width falls from 0.1305 to 0.0895, coverage falls from 70.83% to 66.53%, and pinball loss rises from 0.01694 to 0.01785. Exact GP amplitude and preserved rank ordering do not establish useful uncertainty for this allocator. The borrowed quantile-moment and marginal/dependence constructions operated, but their constant-tail, full-coordinate molecular adaptation does not inherit a performance guarantee.

The method still repeatedly produces aromatic amide, amine and lactam series, with uneven scaffold exploration and more chemically unproductive size extremes: tiny purchases rise from 23 to 191 and very large purchases from 112 to 263. In the docking population, typed/generic scaffold coverage contracts from 507/382 to 266/181, whereas another population expands, so this is not universal scaffold collapse. The molecular assessment associates intact moderate-size motifs with useful scores and identifies fragment collapse, duplicated cores and unusual reactive linkages among poor alternatives. A proposal operator that preserves coherent motifs while changing scaffold or linker topology could address that observed waste; a different uncertainty/ranking model could address the selected-label calibration mismatch. Neither remedy is established here. The passive native-amplitude replay has no alternative scores or feedback history, so it cannot prove which changed purchases mediated the endpoint loss. This result settles the registered amplitude transfer, leaving the wider conditional-quantile approach and retained components open to separately scoped evidence.
finding_summary.results: Transport executed in all 435 allocations and preserved the native standardized shape, GP location, eligibility and correlated random stream. All 69,600 candidate curves had positive variance, and their transported variance matched the original GP variance; no fallback or numerical failure occurred. Compared with native amplitude on the same states, 434 of 435 purchased sets changed, affecting 2,926 of 4,350 purchase positions. Every purchase joined to its accepted score and archive, and all 4,200 nonterminal purchases entered both subsequent fits and next-context probes. Full positive gain over the actual generating parents fell from 16.6861 to 14.3768, although late-half gain rose from 3.9156 to 5.7550. The registered prediction required both gains to increase, so it is refuted by the full-gain loss. The complete endpoint mean also fell from 0.562256 to 0.550785; seed-level changes were +0.003462, -0.024842 and -0.013034. The result remains below the formal Anchor mean of 0.607030 and the unchanged target of 0.609030. The frozen evidence does not include a trusted Child task-safety decision.

molecular.headline: Aromatic, ring-rich offspring include useful amines and lactams, but size extremes, reactive bonds and unspecified stereochemistry persist.
molecular.overall_character: Node n-cfd49808a894 produces predominantly neutral, branched, aromatic polycycles: indole-like carboxamides, N-rich heteroaromatics, lactams, fluorinated imino/carbonyl rings, and aryl groups linked to aliphatic amines. Familiar medicinal-chemistry fragments coexist with N-halogen and O-halogen bonds, cyanate esters, small unsaturated rings, elaborate fused/bridged connectivity, and very large concatenated structures. Synthetic plausibility is therefore questionable overall, not uniformly poor: several high-scoring ordinary amide/amine motifs look approachable, while valence-valid exotic graphs need individual route and stability assessment. No synthesis or physical property measurements were supplied. All five tasks have all three frozen Search seeds, 900 accepted records each including 870 optimizer records; the inspected Child and published code Parent panels are complete, with no missing paths. context.comparison independently reports child_complete=true and paired_complete=true, matched seeds 0/1/2 and no profile mismatch. This report compares that code Parent, n-ada68e100737, and does not substitute the formal Anchor. String-level ring-closure rates span 0.9184 to 0.9736 and aromatic-token rates 0.9069 to 0.9667; these indicate molecules carrying such text, not fractions of atoms. The trajectories show ring-rich output, not missing ring generation. Every accepted optimizer molecule is formally neutral and lacks specified stereocentres; neutral amines are nevertheless common, so charge notation does not establish absent basicity or physiological ionization. RDKit identifies potential stereocentres in 1906/4350 Child optimizer records. Size is uneven: Child versus Parent counts at <=6 heavy atoms are 191/4350 versus 23/4350, and at >=60 are 263/4350 versus 112/4350. The large-size tail is concentrated in one objective. Structural diversity is moderate overall and strongly task dependent: raw typed scaffold variety sometimes rises while generic topology remains concentrated, and tiny structures must not be counted as medicinal-chemistry breadth. Per-task scaffold counts below include the empty Murcko scaffold. Fragment-excluded similarity uses all unordered within-task Morgan radius-2 2048-bit nonchiral Tanimoto pairs of optimizer records with >6 heavy atoms, retaining repeated identities across seeds. These descriptors, counts, and score associations do not judge mechanism activation, component contribution, or selection eligibility. Provenance and exact denominators are in policy/scratch/r0066-00-improve-L01/molecular/molecular-audit.json, derived solely from the frozen request policy/requests/r0066-00-improve-L01-molecular-assess-3705189d8700e1cd.json and its 15 trusted Child staging trajectories plus 15 authoritative published Parent trajectories. That audit records original paths, Search seeds, hashes, and byte-identical run-relative scratch copies. It also distinguishes accepted trajectory records from unobserved or rejected proposals. Transferable gaps belong to this node under this Search panel and budget; chemistry association does not attribute them to the amplitude intervention.

per_task.generated_character: The central population is modest-sized aromatic carboxamide chemistry: median 24 heavy atoms, range 1-48. The seed-1 best (evaluation 241, 0.4330127018922193) is a methoxy/divinyl indole carboxamide linked to pyridine, with 24 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings. Seed 2 instead reaches 0.436818201428663 at evaluation 224 with a 25-heavy-atom sulfur-containing unsaturated fused bicycle bearing an N-bromo aryl carboxamide; related N-fluoro and N-chloro analogues share that score. This is not simple saturated sulfur-ring chemistry. The final seed-2 record remains in that unusual N-halo series at 0.42654444944303593. The Parent likewise explored indole/aryl carboxamides, including N-halogen species. Child/Parent typed/generic scaffold counts are 218/98 versus 210/99; empty-core rows are 23 versus 0. Fragment-excluded mean similarity is 0.235973 across 846 rows/357435 pairs versus 0.245132 across 870 rows/378015 pairs, so extra strings do not imply a major new topological space.
liabilities: N-halogen adjacency occurs in 237/870 Child records versus 130/870 Parent records. N-bromo/N-chloro amides and the extended unsaturated sulfur ring deserve stability and route scrutiny; these are structural alerts, not measured reaction rates.

The high-scoring carboxamide cores are aromatic and comparatively flat; many substitutions alter reactive functionality more than the underlying scaffold. Small inorganic fragments and linked near-duplicates waste chemical complexity at opposite extremes.
missing_features: More consistent preservation of compact aromatic carboxamide topology is missing at the small- and large-size extremes: 24/870 Child records have <=6 heavy atoms versus 0/870 Parent records.

A chemically conservative alternative to repeated N-halogen decoration is underrepresented within the leading sulfur-containing series; the high-scoring ordinary NH-amide example shows such bonds are not necessary for an appreciable observed score. Whether replacing them improves the optimum is unmeasured.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The observed gradient favors retaining a compact fused aromatic/heteroaromatic body plus an aryl carboxamide over fragment collapse or duplication. The 48-heavy-atom linked structure at seed 2 evaluation 127 scores 5.566818963417039e-18; BrBr at evaluation 246 scores 0.0. Both lie far below the compact carboxamides. High scores do not exclude N-halogen bonds, so their occurrence is not evidence of makeability. The Parent's seed-2 best was 0.4619578459378901, above the Child's best in that seed, despite sharing this broad aromatic-amide chemistry; the supplied data do not identify a required missing pharmacophore.

per_task.generated_character: This population has the broadest size tail: median 49 heavy atoms, range 1-120, with 240/870 records at >=60 heavy atoms versus 73/870 for the Parent. Seed 1 gives a 37-heavy-atom, four-aromatic-ring lead at evaluation 267 (0.619191512221327): an N/O-rich fused heterocycle, substituted biaryl/azaaryl rings, a vinyl thioether, aldehyde, two O-C#N cyanates, and an O-Cl substituent. The other seeds retain much larger decorated N-rich carbonyl/thiocarbonyl systems; the seed-2 best at evaluation 292 contains 60 heavy atoms, hydrazone/imine and carbamate/amide linkages, alkynes and N-F. Late seed-2 structures continue duplicating these units. Child/Parent typed/generic scaffold counts are 383/291 versus 382/290, with 71 versus 7 empty cores. Fragment-excluded similarity falls to 0.195225 across 811 rows/328455 pairs from 0.233015 across 864 rows/372816 pairs, but this occurs alongside both size extremes and is not proof of useful diversity.
liabilities: O-Cl is hypochlorite connectivity, not an aryl chloride; O-C#N is a cyanate ester, not a conventional directly attached nitrile. Their occurrence together with an aldehyde and imino heterocycles makes the leading structure a questionable synthetic/stability proposition.

59/870 Child records have <=6 heavy atoms versus 6/870 Parent records. The opposing >=60-heavy-atom tail and elaborate late hydrazone/thiocarbonyl assemblies increase route complexity without a monotonic score advantage.
missing_features: The generator does not consistently retain a size-controlled arrangement of connected heteroaromatic decorations: large repeated fragments persist although the best Child example is substantially smaller.

Robust nonreactive connectivity alternatives around the winning heteroaromatic core are insufficiently established. The score does not show that O-Cl or O-C#N functionality is necessary, nor that removing it would preserve the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 37-heavy-atom seed-1 lead scores 0.619191512221327, the 57-heavy-atom seed-0 best 0.6018373451075345, and the 60-heavy-atom seed-2 best 0.5996071053068452. A 120-heavy-atom structure at seed 2 evaluation 189 reaches only 0.5744865993734772. CC#N at seed 1 evaluation 275 is at the 0.5 floor. Thus intact substituted heteroaromatic connectivity is associated with improvement over fragments, while simple enlargement does not track the best scores. The Parent's seed-2 best is 0.6324541616056452 with 52 heavy atoms. These are independently adapted, confounded structures, not a matched edit experiment; cyanate or hypochlorite benefit cannot be isolated.

per_task.generated_character: The higher-scoring chemistry is aryl-rich and amine-bearing, with meaningful saturated carbon content: median 32 heavy atoms overall, and seed-best structures of 35, 27 and 31 heavy atoms. Seed 0 links substituted phenyl/phenoxy groups through a partially unsaturated N-heterocycle and a benzylic amine substituent. Seed 1 has a fluorene-like aromatic core carrying aminoethyl groups, methoxy/phenol and halogens. Seed 2 gives two aryl groups connected through a pyrroline-like ring and an imidazolidine-like cyclic aminal, with methylthio, phenol, fluoro and bromo substituents. Thus aliphatic/basic-amine-like centres are clearly available; they are not a missing generator capability. The leading cyclic aminal is more chemically delicate than an ordinary all-carbon linker. Child/Parent typed/generic scaffold counts are 266/181 versus 507/382, with 48 versus 1 empty cores. Fragment-excluded similarity rises to 0.178795 across 830 rows/344035 pairs from 0.149041 across 869 rows/377146 pairs, consistent with more concentrated topology here.
liabilities: The leading cyclic aminal and occasional small unsaturated rings need individual chemical scrutiny; high docking-derived scores alone do not establish stable, synthesizable ligands.

The population includes 178/870 O-halogen adjacency flags, compared with 23/870 in the Parent, although the cited seed-best examples avoid that feature. It also includes 40/870 tiny molecules and 21/870 at >=60 heavy atoms. Neutral SMILES with amines must not be interpreted as experimentally determined protonation states.
missing_features: Retention of varied aryl-to-amine ring/linker arrangements is less evident than in the Parent's much broader typed and generic scaffold coverage; amine creation itself is not missing.

Stereochemical specification is absent despite potential centres in 771/870 Child records. This limits chemically defined three-dimensional output; the supplied trajectories do not measure whether stereoisomer resolution would raise the objective.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 31-heavy-atom aromatic aminal/amine structure at evaluation 293 scores 0.9956118042590473; the seed-0 amine-bearing structure scores 0.981720039554138 and the seed-1 aminoethyl fluorene-like structure 0.9393196521587126. The much lower seed-0 evaluation-20 compound, an acetyl pyrrolidine with its nitrogen tied up as an aryl sulfonamide, scores 0.00021169315013374197. These examples associate intact hydrophobic ring systems plus accessible aliphatic amine connectivity with better scores than the small sulfonyl/carbonyl-rich fragments; many edits differ, so no causal pharmacophore assignment follows. The Parent also achieved high scores with aryl/aliphatic amine chemistry: its seed-best values are 0.9999974292469022, 0.9845482536896144 and 0.9937212305252073. No pose or binding measurement is supplied.

per_task.generated_character: The population combines ethoxy/alkyl-substituted aromatic groups with N-rich rings and cyclic amides: median 32 heavy atoms, range 1-64. Seed 0 concentrates on a fused aza-carbazole-like aromatic body attached to an azetidine/exocyclic-alkene system and a larger N-methyl lactam/amine ring. Seed 1 instead retains a biaryl-pyrrole system with a larger cyclic amide. The seed-2 best is a 33-heavy-atom aryl pyrazole-like fused lactam/amine framework plus an unusual O-containing bridged aryl ring. These are substantive polycyclic molecules, not missing aromatic chemistry. Child/Parent typed/generic scaffold counts are 534/385 versus 410/245, with 35 versus 14 empty-core rows. Fragment-excluded mean similarity is 0.215907 across 835 rows/348195 pairs versus 0.241845 across 854 rows/364231 pairs. There is more topology variation in these accepted outputs, though complex ring edits do not establish easier synthesis.
liabilities: Exocyclic alkenes attached to small rings, unusual bridged ether topology, and medium/large N-containing lactams can make synthesis and conformational control difficult; the top score is not a route assessment.

The low-scoring largest example includes an acyl peroxide connection. Tiny-molecule count rises to 35/870 from 16/870 in the Parent, even though the >=60-heavy-atom tail falls to 2/870 from 14/870. Potential centres occur in 390/870 Child records with none specified.
missing_features: A reliable way to preserve the productive aromatic/carbonyl/amine arrangement while changing scaffold topology remains absent from part of the output: ring edits yield both useful variants and fragmented or heavily distorted structures.

Stereochemically defined alternatives and simpler stable ring/linker assemblies are not established among the leading complex polycycles. They are chemistry coverage gaps, not demonstrated objective requirements.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The seed-2 best at evaluation 253 reaches 0.23989882764637246; seed 0 reaches 0.23758356526465807. Both preserve sizable aromatic bodies together with N-methyl carbonyl/amine rings and ethoxy groups. NO at seed 0 evaluation 235 scores 0.0, while a 64-heavy-atom assembly with an acyl peroxide connection at seed 0 evaluation 115 scores only 0.12549527839433483. The final seed-2 molecule, with the N-aryl group replaced by an ethoxy attachment as part of several connectivity differences, scores 0.2081835261246261. Thus the observed higher scores favor keeping a coherent aromatic/polar-ring arrangement rather than deleting it or joining large units through exotic linkers. Parent seed-best values, 0.2338424221286825, 0.23322566212666948 and 0.23666901586613867, occupy the same narrow score band with related N-rich lactam chemistry; no individual missing substituent is isolated.

per_task.generated_character: These molecules largely elaborate N-methyl imino/carbonyl heterocycles with fluorinated carbon groups and aryl or highly fused unsaturated rings: median 27 heavy atoms, range 1-54. Seed 0's best has 25 heavy atoms and three aromatic rings, combining a fluorinated N-rich fused bicycle, one exocyclic imine, one carbonyl, a fluorophenol and a fluoroethyl substituent. Seed 2 instead has a 27-heavy-atom tightly fused/bridged unsaturated system, imino nitrogens and a fluorinated ketone side chain. Seed 1 has another constrained fused N-rich bicycle attached to a fluorinated unsaturated hydroxy ring. Child/Parent typed/generic scaffold counts are 267/158 versus 343/156, with 37 versus 0 empty cores. Fragment-excluded similarity is 0.201568 across 837 rows/349866 pairs versus 0.221432 across 870 rows/378015 pairs; generic topology coverage is nearly unchanged despite a different distribution of typed rings.
liabilities: The digest's cumulated-double-bond text rate is 0.1333, and a cited high-scoring molecule has an allene. Other leading structures have tightly fused small unsaturated rings; these warrant geometry and route scrutiny without assuming every allene is intrinsically unmakeable.

N-halogen adjacency occurs in 184/870 Child records, and the late cited N-chloro imine illustrates that reactive-looking substitution is not consistently rewarded. There are 33/870 <=6-heavy-atom records versus 0/870 Parent records. No >=60-heavy-atom molecules occur, but the 54-heavy-atom worst example shows that adverse size effects can occur below that descriptive cutoff.
missing_features: The generator lacks consistent control of moderate-sized fluorinated polar-ring architectures: oversized replication, fragmentation and extensive heteroatom rewiring remain alongside the more productive compact structures.

Stereochemical and tautomer/protonation-state definition is not established for the fluoroalkyl centres and imino heterocycles. Potential stereocentres occur in 567/870 Child records and none are specified; the supplied score comparisons do not test the benefit of resolving them.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The 25-heavy-atom seed-0 lead at evaluation 290 scores 0.542718174422174; the 27-heavy-atom seed-2 best reaches 0.5024203103030557. A 54-heavy-atom repeated polycycle at seed 1 evaluation 78 scores 1.614303251832256e-29, and tiny fragments are also extremely low. An allene-containing seed-0 analogue at evaluation 213 nevertheless scores 0.4999143952261739. A late N-chloro-imine fused variant at seed 2 evaluation 296 drops to 0.10350096595358946. These data associate moderate size and particular fluorinated imino/carbonyl connectivity with higher values, but do not identify fluorine count, allene content or any single bond as the cause. The Parent's seed-1 best, 0.6054215806683655, is another fluorinated imino heterocycle with small unsaturated rings; greater score did not mean chemically ordinary topology.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-cfd49808a894 under the frozen three-Search-seed, 300-observation sessions, <=6-heavy-atom records total 191/4350 versus 23/4350 for code Parent n-ada68e100737; >=60-heavy-atom records total 263/4350 versus 112/4350. The full trajectories show both tiny fragments and concatenated multi-core structures far below compact high-scoring molecules. These are accepted-output associations and do not identify which component caused the tails.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator does not consistently maintain coherent molecular size and connected functional motifs across accepted offspring.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic proposal capability should preserve connected ring/linker/functional-group arrangements during size changes and obtain feedback on size-controlled alternatives. Neither tail threshold is an inferred universal optimum or authority for a new fixed size filter. Retain the original node, panel and budget when transferring this finding.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Under this node and its code-Parent comparison, leading and late molecules include N-halogen bonds, O-halogen bonds, O-C#N cyanate esters, imines/hydrazones, an acyl-peroxide-linked large structure, and tightly fused unsaturated small rings. Some flagged compounds have high observed scores while others are poor. N-halogen prevalence decreases in some populations and increases in another, so no uniform Child-versus-Parent improvement or deterioration is established.
transferable_gaps.gap: Chemical graph validity does not consistently coincide with stable, synthetically conventional functional-group connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Provide chemically interpretable edits that distinguish carbon-bound halogen or nitrile groups from heteroatom-bound reactive alternatives and can preserve useful ring geometry without exotic linkage formation. Such alternatives require task-local paid feedback and separate route/stability assessment; high score alone cannot certify them and broad forbidden-substructure claims are unsupported.

transferable_gaps.evidence: All 4350 accepted Child optimizer SMILES have zero specified stereocentres, while RDKit identifies potential centres in 1906 records; the Parent also has none specified, with potential centres in 1834/4350. Leading molecules contain substituted saturated rings, benzylic centres, cyclic aminals and fluoroalkyl centres. All records are formally neutral, but many contain amine-like nitrogens, so absence of charge notation is not absence of basic centres.
transferable_gaps.gap: The generator provides essentially no stereochemical specification despite substantial stereogenic connectivity.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Explore a task-agnostic capability to represent and preserve stereochemical identity, and distinguish plausible tautomer/protonation states when relevant, rather than treating every neutral unspecified graph as one fully defined chemical entity. The current evidence establishes missing representation, not a proven score gain from stereoisomer or charge-state enumeration.

transferable_gaps.evidence: For n-cfd49808a894 versus n-ada68e100737 at the same frozen Search scope, one population contracts from 507/382 typed/generic Murcko scaffold categories to 266/181, while another expands from 410/245 to 534/385; empty cores are included. Fragment-excluded pairwise similarity moves in opposite directions in those populations. High-scoring examples repeatedly retain aryl-amide, aryl-amine or N-rich lactam arrangements, even when raw graph edits add unusual rings.
transferable_gaps.gap: Scaffold exploration is uneven and does not consistently provide distinct stable topologies around productive functional-group arrangements.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Support de novo scaffold and linker alternatives that retain coherent polar/hydrophobic group arrangements and evaluate their utility from current-session feedback. Separate true topology variation from heteroatom relabeling, fragment collapse and duplicated cores. Do not prescribe one scaffold, infer universal diversity benefit, or attribute these associations to the registered selector intervention.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
